common_name: Grey Witch Daylily (Gray-Lavender Spider, Parent of Ocean Spirit)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by Reed in 1999, opens narrow, near-spider-form flowers in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by Reed in 1999 from a cross of Trahlyta and an unknown pollen parent, Grey Witch is a dormant diploid bearing gray-lavender flowers about six inches across with a purple eye above a green throat, its narrow petals approaching spider form at a 4.22-to-1 ratio. Carried on 30-inch scapes with 15 buds across two branches, it blooms in the early midseason and earned an AHS Honorable Mention in 2005 followed by an Award of Merit in 2009. It was later used in a cross with Magic of Oz, and that result crossed again with Loch Ness Monster, to produce J.P. Murphy's 2006-registered unusual-form cultivar Ocean Spirit. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Minted Gold Daylily (Fragrant Gold Self, Parent of Commandment)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this fragrant, reblooming dormant tetraploid, registered by Reckamp in 1968, opens a gold self flower in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by Reckamp in 1968 from a complex cross tracing back through Shooting Star, Betty Rice, and Crestwood Ann, Minted Gold is a fragrant, reblooming dormant tetraploid bearing a gold self flower on scapes about 28 inches tall that open in the early midseason. It carries no AHS awards of its own, but its breeding value came through as a parent. Reckamp crossed it with the pairing of Summer Splendor and Paris Gown to produce the 1968-registered Commandment, later a grandparent of the 1975 President's Cup winner Sombrero Way. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Summer Splendor Daylily (Apricot-Orange Blend, Parent of Commandment)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this reblooming dormant daylily, registered by Reckamp in 1965, opens apricot-orange blend flowers in midseason.

directions: Registered by Reckamp in 1965 from a cross involving Betty Rice and Early Sunrise, Summer Splendor is a reblooming dormant daylily bearing apricot-orange flowers about seven inches across with light orchid midribs above a green throat, carried on 28-inch scapes that open in midseason. It earned an AHS Honorable Mention in 1971. Reckamp later crossed it with Paris Gown, pairing the result with Minted Gold to produce the 1968-registered Commandment, grandparent of the 1975 President's Cup winner Sombrero Way. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Paris Gown Daylily (Buff-Pink Blend, Parent of Commandment)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this reblooming dormant diploid, registered by Reckamp in 1965, opens buff-pink blend flowers in midseason.

directions: Registered by Reckamp in 1965 from a multi-generation cross tracing back through North Star, Betty Rice, Lady of Northbrook, and Early Sunrise, Paris Gown is a reblooming dormant diploid bearing buff-pink blend flowers with a green throat, about six inches across on 30-inch scapes that open in midseason. Reckamp later crossed it with Summer Splendor, pairing the result with Minted Gold to produce the 1968-registered Commandment, grandparent of the 1975 President's Cup winner Sombrero Way. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Emerald Crown Daylily (Yellow Self, Parent of Copper Lantern)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid, registered by Joiner in 1978, opens a yellow self flower in midseason.

directions: Registered by Joiner in 1978 from a cross of Vick Mulkey and Jakarta, Emerald Crown is a dormant diploid bearing a yellow self flower with a green throat, about six inches across on 28-inch scapes that open in midseason. It earned an AHS Honorable Mention in 1985. Joiner later crossed it with Colonel Simon to produce the 1982-registered Copper Lantern, which went on to parent the 1999 Lenington All-American Award winner Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Colonel Simon Daylily (Fragrant Jonquil Yellow Self, Parent of Copper Lantern)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this fragrant, reblooming evergreen diploid, registered by L. Simon in 1971, opens jonquil-yellow flowers in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by L. Simon in 1971 from a cross of Clarence Simon and Tim Tanner, Colonel Simon is a fragrant, reblooming evergreen diploid bearing jonquil-yellow flowers with a green throat, about seven inches across on 24-inch scapes that open in the early midseason. It collected a Junior Citation in 1971, an Honorable Mention in 1974, and an Award of Merit in 1977. It was later crossed with Emerald Crown to produce the 1982-registered Copper Lantern, which went on to parent the 1999 Lenington All-American Award winner Orange Velvet. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Sanford Show Girl Daylily (Pastel Mauve Double, Parent of Arms Reaching Out)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this reblooming evergreen diploid double, registered by D. Kirchhoff in 1989, opens pastel mauve flowers early in the season.

directions: Registered by D. Kirchhoff in 1989 from a cross of Both Sides Now and Bette Davis Eyes, Sanford Show Girl is a reblooming evergreen diploid double bearing pastel mauve flowers with a wine-red eyezone above a gold throat, about six inches across on 28-inch scapes that open early in the season. It collected a Junior Citation in 1990 and an Honorable Mention in 1994. It was later crossed with Big Kiss to produce the 2004-registered Arms Reaching Out, itself a parent of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain its double form.

common_name: Double Bow Tie Daylily (Pink-Beige Double, Parent of Beware the Wizard)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this semi-evergreen double daylily, registered by J. Miles in 1969, opens pink-beige flowers in midseason on tall scapes.

directions: Registered by J. Miles in 1969, Double Bow Tie is a semi-evergreen double daylily bearing pink-beige flowers with a maroon eyezone above a green throat, about seven inches across on tall 36-inch scapes that open in midseason. It carries no AHS awards of its own, but its breeding value came through as a parent. G. Couturier later crossed it with Firestorm to produce the 1995-registered Beware the Wizard, itself a parent of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Firestorm Daylily (Brick Red Unusual-Form Crispate, Parent of Beware the Wizard)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this dormant diploid unusual-form daylily, registered by Krekler in 1979, opens brick-red, crispate-petaled flowers in the early midseason.

directions: Registered by Krekler in 1979, Firestorm is a dormant diploid unusual-form daylily with crispate, quilled petals in brick red above a gold-olive throat, each bloom about eight and a quarter inches across on 31-inch scapes that open in the early midseason. It went on to earn an AHS Honorable Mention in 2009, three decades after its introduction. G. Couturier later crossed it with Double Bow Tie to produce the 1995-registered Beware the Wizard, itself a parent of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Ruby Sentinel Daylily (Fragrant Ruby Red Self, Parent of Cherry Valentine)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this fragrant dormant tetraploid, registered by Benz in 1991, opens a ruby-red self flower in the mid-to-late season.

directions: Registered by Benz in 1991 from a cross of Illini Show Girl and Ed Marshall, Ruby Sentinel is a fragrant dormant tetraploid bearing a ruby-red self flower with an emerald-green throat, about five inches across on tall 36-inch scapes that open in the mid-to-late season. It earned an AHS Honorable Mention in 2000. It was later crossed with Enchanting Blessing, and that result crossed again with Dragon's Eye, to produce Trimmer's 1999-registered Cherry Valentine, itself a parent of the 2009 President's Cup winner Mary Alice. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Enchanting Blessing Daylily (Peach-Pink Blend, Parent of Cherry Valentine)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this evergreen diploid, registered by W.M. Spalding in 1983, opens a peach-pink blend flower in midseason on compact scapes.

directions: Registered by W.M. Spalding in 1983, Enchanting Blessing is an evergreen diploid bearing a peach-pink blend flower with a green throat, about five and a quarter inches across on compact 19-inch scapes that open in midseason. It earned an AHS Honorable Mention in 1987 followed by an Award of Merit in 1990. It was later crossed with Ruby Sentinel, and that result crossed again with Dragon's Eye, to produce Trimmer's 1999-registered Cherry Valentine, itself a parent of the 2009 President's Cup winner Mary Alice. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Big Kiss Daylily (Fragrant Light Peach Double, Parent of Arms Reaching Out)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil; this fragrant, reblooming dormant diploid double, registered by Joiner in 1991, opens light peach flowers in midseason.

directions: Registered by Joiner in 1991 from a cross of Dublin Elaine and Frances Joiner, Big Kiss is a fragrant, reblooming dormant diploid double bearing light peach flowers with a light rose eyezone above a light green throat, about five and a half inches across on 28-inch scapes that open in midseason. It earned an AHS Honorable Mention in 2002 followed by an Award of Merit in 2005. It was later crossed with Sanford Show Girl to produce the 2004-registered Arms Reaching Out, itself a parent of the Ida Munson Award winner Mayor of Cornatzer. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain its double form.
